papers.title: Propensity Straight-Through Gradients for Discrete Stochastic Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the propensity straight-through (PST) estimator for gradient-based learning through exact simulations of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs). These models describe discrete stochastic dynamics across physics, chemistry, and biology, but their categorical event choices prevent ordinary differentiation. PST preserves exact forward trajectories and differentiates, in the backward pass, the normalized reaction propensities the simulator already computes. The affine state update makes this rule exact for the one-step conditional-mean sensitivity. We derive the per-step discrepancy for one-step sensitivities composed along nonlinear trajectories in closed form, show that it vanishes for affine downstream dependence, and bound it quadratically in the stoichiometric jump size. Across reversible dimerization, a genetic oscillator, a 50-task repressilator suite, and experimental patch-clamp recordings, PST recovers parameters to within 0.06-1.7% and converges 2.4-3.0-fold faster than the Gumbel-Softmax straight-through estimator at matched computational cost. At deep-learning scale, PST trains all 203,796 parameters of a stochastic reaction network using exact discrete events from initialization. By differentiating an exact conditional mean, PST eliminates reaction-selection temperature tuning and provides a scalable route to learning through exact stochastic dynamics.

papers.title: Orchestra: Corroboration-Based Regulatory Candidate Discovery via Composed Bioinformatics MCP Agents
papers.abstract: Orchestra composes two independently built bioinformatics MCP servers -- RegNetAgents, which infers regulatory network topology, and CASCADE, which provides independent functional evidence (LINCS knockdown, DepMap essentiality, super-enhancer status, DoRothEA transcription-factor confidence) -- into one multi-agent LangGraph workflow. Its central claim is that requiring the two systems to agree on a candidate regulator yields a more trustworthy candidate than either alone. We test this on the TCGA tumor-acquired regulator tier, selecting each query's ten regulators by ARACNe mutual-information edge weight. Across BRCA/COAD focal genes and matched negative controls, requiring at least 2 of 4 evidence sources predicts known-driver status (IntOGen) among focal genes (odds ratio 3.15, Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p=0.016; 2.92 after deduplication) but shows no association among negative controls (p=0.70); a single source does not in BRCA/COAD. In a second panel (STAD) the pattern reproduces and is stronger (OR 6.71, adjusted p=0.0047), again with no association in controls. Corroboration adds value beyond MI edge weight in both panels (BRCA/COAD p=0.039; STAD p=0.0001), though modestly in BRCA/COAD. Deduplication, a permutation test and a reproduction of RegNetAgents' published results agree; a second, separately derived driver list (Vogelstein et al. 2013) is directionally consistent but too sparse to reach significance. All experiments invoke Orchestra's real agentic entry point.

papers.title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
papers.abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

papers.title: Evidence-informed dynamic modelling and intervention prioritisation in diabetic bone marrow
papers.abstract: Aims. Fragmented understanding of how diabetes disrupts interconnected bone marrow niches has hindered integrated strategies to restore function. Building on a previous static network, we developed a dynamic model to simulate intervention responses. Methods. The investigator and ChatGPT dialogued to extract evidence from a frozen corpus and develop the model. A Python implementation extended Boolean logic to three ordinal levels (0, 1 and 2) representing biological states and, where applicable, intervention strength. Under high metabolic stress, 15 interventions were assessed at three strengths and four with binary settings; 171 pairs were tested at maximal strength. A domain balanced score (0 to100) integrated favourable and adverse changes. Staged simulations assessed withdrawal; regulatory constraints on recovery after metabolic stress reduction were examined separately. Results. Endothelial reactive oxygen species (ROS) suppression achieved the highest score among 19 single interventions (24.2), improving three functional domains. Endothelial protein kinase B (Akt) augmentation scored 15.2 (two domains); oncostatin M (OSM) blockade and haematopoietic 66 kDa SHC transforming protein 1 (p66Shc) loss each scored 13.6 (two domains). ROS suppression combined with either OSM blockade or p66Shc loss scored 37.9, (five domains). No pair restored all functions under high stress. Benefits of ROS suppression, Akt augmentation and ROS and OSM blockade disappeared after withdrawal. Reducing metabolic stress led to variable scores (range 4.5 to 100), increasing mainly with restored endothelial function, followed by progenitor recovery and interruption of inflammatory and adipocyte stromal signalling. Conclusions. These simulations offer a rule based framework for investigating diabetic marrow recovery. Experimental studies must establish whether it can guide targeted therapy.
